beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't tell if your agent is safe from its output.
beats.got: You can't see from the answer whether the agent is safe, so you check it.

beats.trigger: Prework covers personal skills and agent risk layered on normal security.
beats.got: nothing new. A list of reading I did not do.

beats.trigger: **Apply** named agent risk patterns (direct and indirect prompt injection, secrets in context, tool confusion, skill supply chain) and a plain access review
beats.got: nothing new. Long English words and no example.

beats.trigger: Name what you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: Think about what I would check before it goes to a real person. Depot managers, for me.

beats.trigger: A tool call is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: The agent writes text and something then does the thing. I did not follow much more.

beats.trigger: Would you bet your job on it being safe?
beats.got: You never get certainty that it is safe. Fine, same as with a driver.

beats.trigger: Classical software security is a risk-based practice, and the software it protects is deterministic: same input, same output.
beats.got: Old software gives the same answer every time. IT stuff.

beats.trigger: Same prompt, same files, same tools, different session, different answer.
beats.got: The agent can give a different answer on the same job, like two drivers on the same route. A text in a document can steer it.

beats.trigger: Scope (give the agent less). Split (two agents, different trust levels). Filter (post-process output). Gate (human approves). Review (a second agent judges).
beats.got: Five ways to make it safer. I only understand 'give less' and 'human approves'.

beats.trigger: "I can't tell" is a real answer.
beats.got: You write down the risk that is left and decide to accept it. Like a depot risk assessment.

beats.trigger: More context makes a good answer likelier. Less access makes a bad answer smaller.
beats.got: Give it fewer rights and a mistake does less damage. That I know from the depot.

beats.trigger: Should the agent have write access to that system?
beats.got: Do not give it write access if it does not need it. Simple.

beats.trigger: Damn, this is complex stuff.
beats.got: nothing new. It is complex and you keep doing the loop.

beats.trigger: A **skill** packages an expertise (rules, checklists, the moves an agent runs) into something the agent loads when the work matches.
beats.got: A skill is a saved checklist the agent can use again. I don't have a company policy folder like this.

beats.trigger: Read the first few rows: they show which rules files can check and which need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: The agent made a table of rules. Some it can check, some not. Okay, it is doing something at least.

beats.trigger: the customer your CEO would not want named in a transcript
beats.got: I just tell it in plain words what is sensitive: driver data, customer contracts. That I can do.

beats.trigger: Expect many questions; the agent keeps probing both lenses over several rounds.
beats.got: The agent asks a lot of questions and writes a check file. Many rounds, long English.

beats.trigger: *"You choose. Optimise for what I can't steer."*
beats.got: When I don't know, I tell it to decide. Good, I will use that.

beats.trigger: Run `ls .claude/skills/agent-audit/` to confirm.
beats.got: Save it, then check that the folder exists. IT work.

beats.trigger: The policy files are source material.
beats.got: nothing new. The check is saved and gets used next time.

beats.trigger: The goal is the loop (assess, mitigate, reassess residual), not a clean bill of health.
beats.got: We run the check on the system from before. It will not come out clean.

beats.trigger: Type `/` and look for `/agent-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: Type slash and the saved check shows up. Easy.

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: It found things I did not think of and said 'cannot tell' on some. That is honest, I like it.

beats.trigger: The uncomfortable feeling is the evidence.
beats.got: The risk list made me a bit uneasy. A document could tell the agent what to do.

beats.trigger: Pick one risk from the two reports: the one that bugs you on the second skim.
beats.got: I picked one risk, the agent fixed it, and the risk that was left was written down. Doable.

beats.trigger: The narrow question the expert can answer is sitting in the report.
beats.got: If I don't know, I take the report to IT or legal with one clear question.

beats.trigger: Risk control, done for every risk you found, separates a prototype from a production agent.
beats.got: We did one risk. A real system needs all of them. Lots of work.

beats.trigger: The reusable check is the expert in the room, and it carries to the next agent.
beats.got: The check can be used again on the next agent.

beats.trigger: *"that residual is too vague, name the file or behaviour."*
beats.got: The agent writes rules for next time and I can correct it if it is vague.

beats.trigger: Others: reviewing customer data use, preparing a weekly briefing, checking source quality, drafting in a house style, triaging a queue.
beats.got: A skill could do my weekly briefing. Maybe the reporting.

beats.trigger: - "I can't tell" is a real answer.
beats.got: nothing new. Short list, good.

beats.trigger: Without the two sentences, you'll be writing them while the rest of the room is already comparing detectors.
beats.got: Homework. I will not do it.

beats.trigger: Read Mata v. Avianca (2023) and Deloitte Australia / DEWR report (2025) in the lecture.
beats.got: nothing new. Two court and consulting cases to read, not my world.

take_homes: Give the agent less access. If it does not need to write, don't let it.
When something is not clear, the check says 'cannot tell' and I take it to IT or legal.
A text in a document can steer the agent, so I check what it reads, not only what it says.

monday.move: Nothing on the AI side. Maybe ask IT whether the reporting tool can be exported, so I could try one report with an agent later.
monday.stop_condition: IT says no or it takes more than a day
monday.blocker: No time, and the reporting system cannot be exported without IT.

misconception.why: The weekly briefing and queue triage examples sounded like operations work, not a customer chatbot. But the whole module used a software system, so I am not convinced for my depots.

one_line: Okay if you build agents, but for me too much talk and no depot example. The 'give it less access' idea was good.
